findings.governingReading: Illya reminds Taiga that she is the assistant instructor or deputy master.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Taiga to the dojo’s master and disrupts the recurring rank joke.

findings.governingReading: Taiga abruptly switches into conspicuous Kansai-flavored speech.
findings.explanation: The English gives her ordinary colloquial speech, leaving Illya’s question about the dialect without an audible trigger.

findings.governingReading: Taiga would rejoice at meeting a real, live dojo challenger before she dies.
findings.explanation: The English loses the comic “live specimen” phrasing that powers the desert-vending-machine comparison.

findings.highlight: the name of this dead end
findings.evidenceJa: デッドエンドのブロック名
findings.governingReading: Taiga says even the block name assigned to this dead end gives her a bad feeling.
findings.explanation: The English omits the game-structural block reference.

findings.evidenceJa: こういう正体がないの
findings.governingReading: Taiga cannot cope with an attacker lacking a definite identity or form.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes her specific fear of the formless into dislike of mysterious things.

findings.governingReading: Taiga points the shadow toward the girl in gym bloomers.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the clothing term untranslated, weakening the visual contrast with the hakama.

findings.highlight: Her moe power is ten times stronger than mine
findings.evidenceJa: 萌え指数でいけば優にわたしの十倍はあろうか強キャラ
findings.governingReading: Taiga sells Illya as a formidable character whose appeal index is easily ten times hers.
findings.explanation: The English turns comic attractiveness plus character strength into a single “moe power” combat statistic.

findings.evidenceJa: グルメな貴方も根こそぎにございます
findings.governingReading: Taiga recommends Illya as something the gourmet shadow can consume root and branch.
findings.explanation: The English removes the attempted sacrificial consumption and substitutes satisfaction.

findings.evidenceJa: タイガもさるもの、段々と開き直ってきた
findings.governingReading: The commentary says Taiga is no slouch and is gradually settling into brazen acceptance.
findings.explanation: The English removes the praise and reduces the comic adaptation to defiance.

findings.highlight: You’ll just end up losing even if you fight that thing
findings.evidenceJa: あんなのとマトモに戦っても負けるだけ
findings.governingReading: A direct or head-on fight with the shadow can only end in defeat.
findings.explanation: The English warns against fighting generally and loses the tactical qualification.

findings.evidenceJa: 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず
findings.governingReading: Nothing ventured, nothing gained—literally, one cannot take a tiger cub without entering its den.
findings.explanation: The English changes dangerous entry for a desired prize into enduring pain and loses the Tiger Dojo image.

findings.evidenceJa: へいレフリー、ワタシたっぷしてるネー
findings.governingReading: Taiga abruptly performs broken pseudo-foreign referee speech while tapping out.
findings.explanation: The English conveys surrender but normalizes the conspicuous voice shift.

findings.evidenceJa: わたしが師範代になってる
findings.governingReading: Illya jokes that she may be the assistant instructor next time if things go well.
findings.explanation: The English again promotes the assistant-instructor role to dojo master.
